name: autoconf
description: The Autoconf package contains programs for producing shell scripts that can automatically configure source code.

installed_descriptions.name: autoconf
installed_descriptions.description: Produces shell scripts that automatically configure software source code packages to adapt to many kinds of Unix-like systems; the configuration scripts it produces are independent—running them does not require the autoconf program

installed_descriptions.name: autoheader
installed_descriptions.description: A tool for creating template files of C #define statements for configure to use

installed_descriptions.name: autom4te
installed_descriptions.description: A wrapper for the M4 macro processor

installed_descriptions.name: autoreconf
installed_descriptions.description: Automatically runs autoconf, autoheader, aclocal, automake, gettextize, and libtoolize in the correct order to save time when changes are made to autoconf and automake template files

installed_descriptions.name: autoscan
installed_descriptions.description: Helps to create a configure.in file for a software package; it examines the source files in a directory tree, searching them for common portability issues, and creates a configure.scan file that serves as a preliminary configure.in file for the package

installed_descriptions.name: autoupdate
installed_descriptions.description: Modifies a configure.in file that still calls autoconf macros by their old names to use the current macro names

installed_descriptions.name: ifnames
installed_descriptions.description: Helps when writing configure.in files for a software package; it prints the identifiers that the package uses in C preprocessor conditionals [If a package has already been set up to have some portability, this program can help determine what configure needs to check for. It can also fill in gaps in a configure.in file generated by autoscan.]
